result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers separate the acceptable parts from the problems, flag the same core issues and rank phone-only cancellation as the worst. A wins because it gives fuller fixes, including replacement wording for a whole screen (heading, end-date copy, equal-weight buttons, optional reason). A also questions the 3x stat on correlation grounds. A's legal paragraph is weaker: it calls the flow 'not legal' until the call, and it cites the FTC click-to-cancel approach without noting the rule was struck down. B's legal summary is more accurate, but its fixes stop at button labels. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers separate the acceptable parts from the unacceptable ones, rank the phone-only cancellation as the worst problem, and catch the buried link and the lopsided buttons. B is better because it writes out a full replacement screen with exact wording, and it explains why the '3x' claim may not mean what it implies (members who stay longer are probably the more motivated ones). A's fixes are mostly directives with little replacement copy. Neither invents statistics. A's legal claims are specific but accurate. B's legal sentences are muddled: 'isn't legal until the call happens' is garbled, and it presents the FTC's click-to-cancel approach as a current requirement even though the rule was struck down in 2025.
